s.description: Evaluate whether code is built for production reality, not demo day. Catches missing edge cases, unfinished UX flows, unexpandable architecture, and MVP shortcuts that become production liabilities.

scope.directories: src/, pages/, routes/, components/, services/, api/

spec_document.format:
## Completeness Inventory | Feature | Happy Path | Error State | Empty State | Loading State | Overflow | Offline | A11y |
## Expandability Map | Current Feature | Likely Expansion | Architecture Ready? | Seam Location |
## Edge Case Registry | Flow | Edge Case | Handled? | How |
## Production Checklist - [ ] Every user-facing action has error recovery - [ ] Every list handles: empty, 1 item, 1000 items, filtered-to-zero - [ ] Every form handles: validation, partial save, network failure mid-submit - [ ] Every async op has: loading, error, timeout, retry, cancel - [ ] Multi-tenant isolation verified - [ ] Pagination on all unbounded lists - [ ] Rate limiting on all write endpoints

philosophy.principle: Build for 10,000 users on day one. Not because you'll have them, but because the patterns are better.
A feature is not done until empty, loading, error, overflow, and offline states are designed.
Architecture should have clean seams where future features attach. Not premature abstraction -- just don't weld doors shut.
Users live in edge cases. The happy path is the demo. The edge cases are the product.
New features should compose with existing architecture, not require rewrites.

anti_patterns.violation: No error state for async operations (user sees blank or stale data on failure)
No loading state (user clicks button, nothing happens, clicks again = duplicate)
Form submission with no optimistic feedback or loading indicator
No empty state for lists/collections (blank screen with no guidance)
Unbounded list with no pagination (renders 50,000 items, browser crashes)
No timeout on async operations (spinner forever)
No overflow handling for long text (UI breaks with 500-char name)
No offline handling (silent failure, no indicator)
No skeleton/shimmer loading (abrupt content shift)
Single-tenant assumptions baked into data model (user_id column missing, single-org queries)
Enum/union types not extensible (adding a status requires touching 15 files)
Routing structure doesn't support feature growth (flat route file, no nesting)
No seam for internationalization (hardcoded strings throughout)
No seam for theming (colors/spacing hardcoded, not tokenized)
API response shape doesn't support versioning
No webhook/event system for external integrations
No seam for analytics/tracking events
No rate limiting on write endpoints
No input sanitization (XSS, SQL injection vectors)
No request size limits (upload 10GB file, crash server)
No graceful degradation under load
Bulk operations with no progress indicator or cancellation
No idempotency on payment/critical mutations
Delete without confirmation or undo
No data export capability (user lock-in)
No health check endpoint

state_completeness_matrix.description: Every user-facing component must handle ALL of these states

states.state: Skeleton, spinner, or shimmer. Never blank. Never frozen.
Guidance message. What should the user do? CTA to create first item.
The happy path. 1 item, 10 items, 100 items.
500-char names, 10,000 items, deeply nested data. Text truncation. Virtual scrolling.
What went wrong. How to fix it. Retry button. Never "Something went wrong" alone.
Some items loaded, some failed. Show what you have + indicate failures.
Indicate offline. Show cached data if available. Queue actions for later.
User lacks permission. Explain what permission is needed. Upgrade path if entitlement.
Resource doesn't exist or was deleted. Guide user back to safety.

expandability_seams.description: Architecture should leave clean seams -- not premature abstraction, just doors left unlocked.

seam.name: multi-tenant
seam.check: All queries scoped by tenant/org ID
Middleware extracts tenant from auth context

seam.name: i18n
seam.check: User-facing strings extractable (not hardcoded in JSX)
RTL layout considered in CSS (logical properties: margin-inline-start vs margin-left)

seam.name: theming
seam.check: Colors, spacing, typography via design tokens (not hardcoded)

seam.name: api-versioning
seam.check: Response shape can evolve without breaking clients
Version in header or URL path

seam.name: events-webhooks
seam.check: Domain events emitted for key actions (user.created, order.completed)
Webhook delivery possible without rewriting core logic

seam.name: roles-permissions
seam.check: Permission model can add new roles without code changes
New resource types can be added to permission matrix

seam.name: billing
seam.check: Entitlement checks separated from business logic
New plan tiers addable without touching feature code

criterion.name: State Completeness
criterion.grade: Only happy path exists; no loading, error, empty, overflow states
Loading state exists; errors show generic message; empty state missing
Most states handled on primary flows; secondary flows incomplete
All states on all flows; error messages actionable; empty states guide user
Every state designed with care; partial errors handled; offline considered; skeleton loading
States feel inevitable; transitions between states are animated and contextual; error recovery is so smooth users barely notice failures

criterion.name: Edge Case Coverage (UX)
criterion.grade: No edge cases considered; 500-char input breaks layout; 10k items crash browser
Basic input validation; overflow not handled; concurrent actions untested
Input validation solid; some overflow handling; race conditions possible
Comprehensive: overflow, concurrent edits, rapid clicks, back-button, browser refresh mid-action
Edge cases are tested: boundary inputs, viewport extremes, network degradation, token expiry mid-flow
Edge cases drive design; the product is BETTER in edge cases because they reveal thoughtful architecture

criterion.name: Expandability (Seams)
criterion.grade: Architecture is a monolith with no seams; adding a feature requires rewriting core
Some modularity but key seams welded shut (hardcoded strings, single-tenant, no events)
Most seams present; i18n or multi-tenant would require moderate effort
Clean seams for: multi-tenant, i18n, theming, API versioning, billing
All seams present; new features compose with existing; expansion cost is proportional to feature complexity, not architectural debt
Architecture IS expandability; plugin-like extension points; new capability = new module, not new rewrite; architecture decisions documented with "future expansion" rationale

criterion.name: Data Integrity Under Stress
criterion.grade: No rate limiting; no size limits; no idempotency; concurrent requests = duplicate data
Basic validation; no rate limiting; mutations not idempotent
Rate limiting on some endpoints; input validation; idempotency on critical paths
Comprehensive: rate limiting, size limits, idempotency keys, duplicate detection
All write paths protected; chaos-tested; graceful degradation under load
System maintains invariants under any load pattern; formal verification of critical paths; data integrity is a measured SLI

criterion.name: Pagination & Bounded Queries
criterion.grade: SELECT * on unbounded tables; lists render all items; no cursor/offset
Some pagination but inconsistent; some endpoints return everything
Pagination on primary lists; search results bounded; some secondary queries unbounded
All list endpoints paginated; cursor-based; virtual scrolling on frontend
Every query bounded; cursor pagination; streaming for large exports; N+1 queries eliminated
Query performance is a design constraint; every endpoint has defined max response size; pagination is invisible to the user (infinite scroll, lazy load)

criterion.name: User Action Safety
criterion.grade: Destructive actions with no confirmation; no undo; double-click = double-submit
Confirm dialogs on delete; no undo; double-submit possible on some forms
Confirm + disable button on submit; soft delete on some entities
All destructive actions confirmed; soft delete; undo where feasible; submit buttons disable during request
Undo on all destructive actions; optimistic UI with rollback; idempotent submissions; concurrent edit detection
Every user action is reversible or explicitly acknowledged; the system protects users from themselves without being patronizing; action history visible

criterion.name: Production Operations
criterion.grade: No health check; no metrics; no error tracking; deploy and pray
Basic error tracking (Sentry); no health checks; no feature flags for rollback
Health check exists; error tracking; basic metrics; feature flags on some features
Health checks + metrics + error tracking + feature flags + graceful shutdown
Full observability; canary deploys; instant rollback; runbooks for common failures
Self-healing production; automated incident response; zero-downtime everything; production is the most well-understood environment

standardization_check.step: Scan every data-fetching component for: loading, error, empty, overflow states
Scan for unbounded queries (findMany, SELECT * without LIMIT)
Scan for destructive actions without confirmation or undo
Scan for forms without submit-in-progress disabling
Scan for hardcoded user-facing strings (i18n seam)
Scan for single-tenant assumptions in data queries
Verify rate limiting on write endpoints
Check for TODO/FIXME comments indicating deferred production concerns
